newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends firmer as July expires.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends firmer as July expires.

text.p: CSCE sugar futures closed higher in a volatile session that saw the nearby switch trade from 0.25 to 0.01 cent October premium, and then widen to 0.19 cent by the close.
Floor sources attributed the price swing to speculative shortcovering of July contracts ahead of the expiry, and to local trading of the nearby switch.
The spot month went out 0.08 cent firmer at 11.00 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.14 to 10.88 cents. Most-active October settled up 0.05 at 11.19, traded 11.12 to 11.09 cents.
The deferred contracts finished 0.05 cent higher.
Floor sources said the bulk of the day's volume, estimated at only 15,718 lots, centered on the July contract. Friday's official volume was 36,431 lots, CSCE said.

Speculative selling of the July/October spread pressured prices early, but local buying of October contracts in an attempt to probe stops around 11.22 cents in October, carried the market back over unchanged.
Failing to reach its upside target, the benchmark contract eased back toward unchanged in the afternoon. A final run for the stops carried the contract to the day's high of 11.21 cents.
While prices could continue to climb on Tuesday, the heavy open interest in the benchmark October contract has some players worried about a potential selloff.
As of Friday, open interest climbed 1,392 lots to stand at 92,790 lots.

For October sugar, support was pegged at 11.00 cents, followed by the recent low of 10.96 cents and then at 10.80 cents. Resistance was seen at 11.22 cents, followed by 11.34 cents and then 11.50 cents.
Activity should remain quiet for the rest of the week due to Friday's Fourth of July holiday, traders said.
